why: A = theorem_3_27_loc (universe 0) ∧ the four theorem_3_27_loc_* lemmas (universe 0). As in V3_24: every theorem of A assumes regular project data (IsRegular: (a) δ sc-smooth on all of V, (b) π(O) ⊆ C) at every point, B only the blind Definition 3.25 (fixed sc-smooth germ, no condition on π(O)) plus a tame X. (a) is recoverable (convert the blind datum as in V3_22, then exists_isRegular_of_locally shrinks it; its proof of (a) does not use (b)); (b) is the genuine gap: it holds for a suitably chosen complement but not for B's given Y (Finding 83), and changing Y means re-graphing M (an IFT on a partial quadrant), new mathematics; (b) is satisfiable, so A is not vacuous, and whether B holds without (b) is open. B's chart clause is for every datum (A: regular data only) and its fixed dimension n is recoverable from A's chart clause (glue). B ⇒ A fails: A needs no tame X, allows varying dimension, uses k-dependent project germs B does not supply, and its atlas_equiv is about the project's germAtlasLoc.
